name: Claudius Lysias
title: The Roman Tribune in Jerusalem
summary: Claudius Lysias was a Roman military tribune (chiliarch) who commanded the garrison at the Antonia Fortress in Jerusalem. He rescued the apostle Paul from an angry mob in the temple and ensured his safe transfer to Governor Felix in Caesarea. His actions played a crucial role in protecting Paul and securing him fair treatment under Roman law.

keyEvents.title: Rescues Paul from the Mob
keyEvents.description: When an angry mob tried to kill Paul in the temple, Claudius Lysias intervened with soldiers and saved him by arresting and taking him away.

keyEvents.title: Paul is Bound and Interrogated
keyEvents.description: Claudius Lysias ordered Paul to be bound with two chains and attempted to find out who he was and what he had done, but could not get clarity due to the commotion.

keyEvents.title: Discovers Paul's Roman Citizenship
keyEvents.description: When Claudius Lysias intended to have Paul flogged to make him confess, Paul revealed that he was a Roman citizen. The tribune was terrified when he realized he had bound a Roman without a trial.

keyEvents.title: Paul Brought Before the High Council
keyEvents.description: Claudius Lysias brought Paul before the Sanhedrin to determine what the charges against him were, but had to intervene again when a violent dispute broke out between the Pharisees and the Sadducees.

keyEvents.title: Exposing the Murder Plot Against Paul
keyEvents.description: When Claudius Lysias learned of a conspiracy in which more than forty men had sworn to kill Paul, he organized a large military escort to bring Paul safely to Caesarea during the night.

keyEvents.title: Writing a Letter to Governor Felix
keyEvents.description: Claudius Lysias sent a letter to Governor Felix explaining the circumstances surrounding Paul's arrest and transfer, and portrayed himself in a favorable light by claiming that he had rescued Paul because he knew Paul was a Roman citizen.
